newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - FTSE to steer slow course to 4,590-4,600.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - FTSE to steer slow course to 4,590-4,600.

text.p: The FTSE 100 index will try to steer an upward course, aiming for the 4,590-4,600 region on Friday despite a less than enthusiastic start to trading, technical analysts said.
The market's attempt to extend Thursday's 19 point gain will be in thin voloume as investors await a Bank of England decision on UK interest rates and payroll data from the U.S.
But sectors to show relative strength today should include banks, insurance, chemicals and pharmaceuticals.
By 0715 GMT, at the pre-market open, the FTSE was indicated up 2.6 at 4,578.8.

The market had been falling for most of this week so that a significant proportion of traders may still have short positions. If today's economic data is positive for the market, the move to higher ground will be exaggerated by these traders forced to liquidate their short positions.
On the downside, the FTSE first level of support is at 4,530.

The market's direction will mostly hinge on jobs data from the U.S. and consensus forecasts by economists polled by Reuters are for non-farm payrolls for May to have increased by 221,000 and the hourly earnings to have gone up by 0.4 percent.

Significantly, weaker figures will reduce the chances that the Federal Reserve will raise U.S. interest rates in July -- and possibly August -- which will allow Wall Street to resume its bull run over the next couple of months and allow the FTSE to follow suit.
Conversely, stronger than expected jobs data will send both stock markets running for cover, analysts said.
